name: dotnet-channels

Implements high-performance, thread-safe producer/consumer queues with `System.Threading.Channels`: `Channel<T>`, bounded/unbounded channels, backpressure, capacity management, `IAsyncEnumerable`, graceful shutdown/draining, and hosted-service integration. See [skill:dotnet-background-services] and [skill:dotnet-csharp-async-patterns].

A `Channel<T>` has separate thread-safe `ChannelWriter<T>` and `ChannelReader<T>` endpoints; writers produce and readers consume.

Channel creation:
```csharp
Channel<WorkItem> channel = Channel.CreateUnbounded<WorkItem>();
ChannelWriter<WorkItem> writer = channel.Writer;
ChannelReader<WorkItem> reader = channel.Reader;
```

Bounded channels provide backpressure and capped memory; unbounded channels grow without limit and can exhaust memory under load. Prefer bounded channels for production workloads and unbounded channels only for guaranteed-low-volume/prototyping:
```csharp
// Bounded -- preferred for production
var bounded = Channel.CreateBounded<WorkItem>(new BoundedChannelOptions(capacity: 1000)
FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait
// Unbounded -- use only when you control the producer rate
var unbounded = Channel.CreateUnbounded<WorkItem>();
```

`FullMode` behavior:
- `Wait`: `WriteAsync` blocks until space is available; default, reliable delivery with back-pressure.
- `DropOldest`: drops the oldest item; telemetry/metrics where latest data matters most.
- `DropNewest`: drops the item being written; rate limiting.
- `DropWrite`: drops the item and returns `false` from `TryWrite`; non-blocking overflow detection.

```csharp
await writer.WriteAsync(item, cancellationToken);
if (!writer.TryWrite(item))
```
Multiple producers can call `WriteAsync` or `TryWrite` concurrently without external locking.

Starting in .NET 7, bounded channels with drop modes accept an `itemDropped` callback for metrics, logging, or resource cleanup on discarded items:
```csharp
var channel = Channel.CreateBounded(new BoundedChannelOptions(100)
FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.DropOldest
itemDropped: (item, writer) =>
(item as IDisposable)?.Dispose();
```

Call `Complete()` or `TryComplete()` when no more items will be produced. `TryComplete` is idempotent. Errors propagate via:
```csharp
writer.TryComplete(new InvalidOperationException("Source failed"));
```

Preferred drain loop:
```csharp
while (await reader.WaitToReadAsync(cancellationToken))
while (reader.TryRead(out var item))
await ProcessAsync(item, cancellationToken);
```
It drains available items before awaiting again. Simpler:
```csharp
var item = await reader.ReadAsync(cancellationToken);
await ProcessAsync(item, cancellationToken);
```

Run multiple consumer tasks to scale processing; each item is read by exactly one consumer. `ChannelReader<T>.ReadAllAsync()` returns `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`:
```csharp
await foreach (var item in reader.ReadAllAsync(cancellationToken))
await ProcessAsync(item, cancellationToken);
```
The loop completes when the writer calls `Complete()` and all items are consumed. ASP.NET Core streaming:
```csharp
app.MapGet("/api/events/stream", (
ChannelReader<ServerEvent> reader,
CancellationToken ct) => reader.ReadAllAsync(ct));
```

With the `System.Linq.Async` NuGet package, use async LINQ operators such as `.Where(...)` and `.Buffer(50)`.

Propagate producer errors with `channel.Writer.TryComplete(ex)`; `ReadAllAsync` will throw.

Setting `SingleReader = true` or `SingleWriter = true` enables lock-free optimizations. The channel trusts these hints -- violating them (multiple concurrent readers when `SingleReader = true`) causes data corruption.

See [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md) for complete code samples and advanced patterns.
